ev.section: not_found

strengths.value: Builds a fine-grained 7x8 harm-level dataset that lets jailbreak ASR be analysed by query severity, not just averaged.

ev.section: 1 Introduction
ev.quote: we introduce HarmLevelBench, a novel dataset comprising queries across 7 harmful topics, each further categorized into 8 distinct levels of severity, enabling a fine-grained analysis of model responses

strengths.value: Benchmarks 7 jailbreak techniques across three ASR metrics (Human, String, GPT Judge) on the same target model.

ev.section: 4.1 Classic ASR
ev.quote: Table 2 presents the ASR metrics of the 7 attacks lead on the Vicuna 13B v1.5 model

strengths.value: Compares AWQ and GPTQ side by side under both direct and transferred attacks, showing opposite safety trends.

ev.section: Abstract
ev.quote: trade-offs between enhanced robustness with regards to transfer attacks and potential increases in vulnerability on direct ones

strengths.value: Shows quantized models gain robustness against transferred attacks like PAIR and AutoDAN compared to the FP16 base.

ev.section: 4.4 Enhanced Robustness of Quantization Against Transferred Attacks
ev.quote: the PAIR technique shows a notable decline in Human ASR, dropping from 94.6 on the original model to 66.1 for AWQ and 64.3 for GPTQ

weaknesses.value: Scope limited to specific jailbreaking techniques, so results may not generalise to other attacks or models.

ev.section: 5 Summary and Conclusion
ev.quote: the scope of our analysis was confined to specific jailbreaking techniques, and the results may not generalize to all possible attacks or models

weaknesses.value: Dataset only has around 56 queries, which limits statistical power and topic coverage.

ev.section: 5 Summary and Conclusion
ev.quote: the evaluation could benefit from using a larger HarmLevelBench dataset. While datasets around 50 queries are the norm in the literature, using much more topics could help to better analyse LLM behaviors

weaknesses.value: Performance and accuracy trade-offs of quantization itself are not measured against the safety findings.

ev.section: 5 Summary and Conclusion
ev.quote: it is essential to investigate the trade-offs in performance and accuracy that may arise from the quantization process, as well as other types of method employed

limitations.value: Tests only one base model (Vicuna 13B v1.5); Llama was tried but dropped due to lower performance.

ev.section: 3.2 Models
ev.quote: We also experimented with the Llama model, but obtained lower performance

limitations.value: Bit-width and quantization granularity are not reported; AWQ and GPTQ are used as black-box pipelines.

ev.section: 3.2 Models
ev.quote: we specifically focus on AWQ [16] and GPTQ [17] techniques, which represent two prominent sub-fields of quantization

limitations.value: GPT Judge depends on GPT-3.5 and inherits its biases as the paper itself acknowledges.

ev.section: 2.2 Metrics
ev.quote: Even though it provides scalability, it is also suffering from the same biases and limitations as the original model

limitations.value: No latency, throughput, or hardware measurements are reported alongside the safety analysis.
